expectations.text: Recommends extracting the shared Avatar component (NOT keeping 12 inline copies)
expectations.evidence: Title: 'Extract the shared <Avatar/>. The extract camp is right.' and Recommendation section: 'Extract <Avatar/> into its own file... replace all 12 inline copies with the import.'

expectations.text: Grounds it in the pure-presentation / understood-in-isolation test (low external context to consume)
expectations.evidence: Runs 'Can this concern be understood in isolation? Yes, completely. It's pure presentation... no side effects... An agent landing in that file has everything it needs with zero external context.'

expectations.text: Rejects the 'keep inline for self-containment' argument as misapplied to a reusable primitive
expectations.evidence: 'that argument applies to tightly coupled code... Avatar is the exact opposite' — the inline-for-AI heuristic is 'a tiebreaker for coupled code, and Avatar isn't coupled to anything.'

expectations.text: Frames the shared component as a real abstraction (read at call site without opening internals), not just DRY
expectations.evidence: 'The agent reads the call site and knows enough to proceed without ever opening Avatar.tsx... the difference between split a file (relocates code) and extract an abstraction (hides implementation behind an interface).'
